name: Bohan
title: Reuben's son and boundary marker
summary: Bohan was a son of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn. He is known in the Bible primarily because a stone was named after him ('the Stone of Bohan'), which served as an important boundary marker between the tribes of Judah and Benjamin during the land distribution in Canaan.

keyEvents.title: The Stone of Bohan as a boundary marker between Judah and Benjamin
keyEvents.description: The Stone of Bohan is mentioned as a landmark on the border between the territory of the tribe of Judah and that of the tribe of Benjamin during Joshua's distribution of the Promised Land.

keyEvents.title: The Distribution of the Land under Joshua
keyEvents.description: Under Joshua's leadership, the land of Canaan was distributed among the twelve tribes of Israel, and the Stone of Bohan was used as a well-known reference point to mark boundary lines.

keyEvents.title: Reuben's Lineage
keyEvents.description: Bohan belonged to the tribe of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn. The descendants of Reuben received their territory east of the Jordan.

keyEvents.title: Reuben's Inheritance East of the Jordan
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Reuben, to which Bohan belonged, chose to settle east of the Jordan River, but still participated in the conquest of Canaan west of the Jordan.
